heading: # PB-6 · Result
paragraph: **Closed 2026-09-05.** Completed, with the entry's cause corrected by reproduction: cleanup was already content-based (`git merge-tree --write-tree` recognises a plain squash, pinned by a fixture since the snapshot). The real failure needs one more step — after the squash the base moves over the same file, the re-merge conflicts, and the directory of an accepted branch is kept while the report blames "a conflict or an old git". Second measurement added in `lib/worktree.js`: patch identity (`git patch-id --stable` over the branch's diff from its fork point, narrowed to the branch's own paths on both sides, looked for among the commits the base gained since the fork — a squash carries exactly that patch, later commits over the same file do not move it, and a squash that landed inside a wider commit is still recognised). `worktreeDisposition` says `merged as a squash`, `is entirely in <base>` or `is not merged`, and names both comparisons when nothing could be confirmed. `git apply -R --3way` was tried and rejected: it exits 0 with "Applied patch with conflicts" on a branch never merged, and would delete real work. Recognition stays narrow on purpose. Track `cli`, same worker and review round.

heading: # PB-52 · Result
paragraph: **Closed 2026-09-09.** Completed with the owner's choice of the card's first option, recorded as ADR-006. A guard hook group in project settings is recognised as Promptobus's own first by the exact ids of the machine-local install manifest and, when the manifest is absent (a checkout copied from another machine, a deleted `.promptobus/`), by a portable signature of the command the package itself renders — an anchored regex `GUARD_SIGNATURE` in `lib/install.js`: two quoted launch elements, optional bare host-prefix words, the bare `guard` word, then nothing or exactly `--role <value> --task <value> --home <value>` with shell-quoted values — never by this machine's absolute node and binary paths and never by a bare substring. A foreign-path guard is therefore replaced on install and removed on uninstall instead of duplicated and orphaned; wrappers such as `"/bin/sh" "-c" node hook.js guard`, a quoted `guard`, unknown or incomplete tails and unterminated quotes stay foreign. The accepted false-positive class is named in the guides: any Stop/SessionStart (Cursor `stop`) command of that exact shape is treated as ours whatever binary it launches. No committed ownership manifest was added (the rejected alternative); install.md now says the manifest is machine-local state the installer never commits and tells the reader to ignore `.promptobus/`. PB-103's interim needle is gone; `layoutBinPath()` is documented as the entry a host builds `guardArgv` from, no longer called by the package. The card's "keep the bin-path needle as extra confirmation" is superseded by the owner's option: an OR-chained extra term changes nothing. `src/hooks.ts` and `src/standalone.ts` from Scope needed no change — PB-103 already moved the rendered argv into the host.

heading: # PB-131 · Result
paragraph: **Closed 2026-09-09.** Completed. `MESSAGE_TYPES` in `src/protocol.ts` is `Object.freeze`d, so it is immutable at runtime and `readonly string[]` in TypeScript; `MESSAGE_TYPES_V1` in `src/v1/model.ts` is that same object without a separate re-annotation. A JavaScript consumer can enumerate or copy the list but can no longer push a foreign type into it and thereby widen what the record validator and the engine gate accept for the rest of the process. A literal `as const` tuple was tried and rejected within the task's scope: it surfaced three `.includes(string)` type errors that would have needed casts or validator edits, so the frozen array keeps the surgical boundary. `test/mcp.test.mjs`'s `enum: [...MESSAGE_TYPES]` still copies into a plain array and type-checks unchanged. The regression in `test/v1-engine.test.mjs` attempts the mutation from JavaScript and proves the push throws, the length stays 7, and an injected type reaches neither the record validator nor the engine.
